size.note: Adults 4-8 cm snout to vent, to ~15 cm in all, about 3-8 g; the tail constricted at its base, long legs, big protruding eyes. Drawn (the Oregon subspecies, E. e. oregonensis) at 0.055 m snout to vent and a 0.055 m tail (0.11 m straight), the trunk 1.1 cm across, the back 8.7 mm up at mid-body on legs 1.3x the red-backed salamander's, the belly ~1 mm off the ground, toe span 4.1 cm. Mass not in the brief: 5 g taken from the field-guide range. length_m here is total length (snout to tail tip); shoulder_or_wingspan_m is the back's height.

source.prompt: A western red-backed salamander (Plethodon vehiculum), a small slender woodland salamander, NOT a lizard, NOT a newt, no scales, smooth moist skin. One adult walking on the ground, side-on pose, body straight, four short thin legs splayed out to the sides with small toes. Realistic proportions: 10 cm long, the round tapering tail as long as the body, a slender cylindrical body with fine grooves along the sides, a small rounded head a little wider than the neck, small dark bulging eyes. A broad straight-edged reddish-orange stripe down the back from the head to the tail tip, dark grey-black sides with fine white flecks, a grey belly. No base, no ground. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

rig: reptile template, exactly as the western red-backed salamander's (tools/build_salamander.py; the fence lizard's template, drawn by the client with the lizard's spine wave and sprawling walk): BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left fore, right hind) and LEG_B 2 (right fore, left hind) splayed, pivots at the shoulder and hip rings; HEAD 6 (pivot at the neck); TAIL 3 (inner half, pivot at the vent) and TAIL_TIP 8 (outer half, pivot mid-tail, child of TAIL). extras.rig (kind 'reptile'): head, tail, tail_tip, fore, hind, legs (FL FR HL HR), snout_z, vent_z, tail_end_z, belly_y, back_y, drop, blue_off and throat_off (the belly colour; nothing is blue), length_m. No skin.
accuracy_notes: A variant of the red-backed salamander's mesh, no new generation. Reads as an ensatina: stouter and a little bigger than the red-backed (1.1 cm across), long legs (1.3x) that hold it higher, big protruding black eyes with a yellow-cream fleck above each, the tail pinched at its base and swollen behind the pinch, then tapering; plain brown to reddish-brown above finely flecked darker, slightly darker sides, yellowish-orange limb bases (the upper arms and thighs), a pale whitish-yellow belly. Still wrong or unchecked: the shape is the red-backed preview's (a slender plethodontid head, not the ensatina's broader one); the eye bulge is the generator's small eye pushed out 1.45x, so it is big but not quite the ensatina's domed eye; the belly's fine dark specks only fall on small faces and barely show; the tail constriction shows clearly on lod0 and lod1 but not on lod2; only the Oregon subspecies' plain colouring is drawn (no blotched or yellow-eyed forms).
